r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:4: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:5: Advanced Alchemy provides automatic routing of read operations to read replicas while directing
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:6: write operations to the primary database. This enables better scalability by distributing read
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:7: load across multiple replica databases.
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:8: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:9: Why Use Read/Write Routing?
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:10: ----------------------------
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:11: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:12: Read/write routing is essential for scaling read-heavy applications:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:13: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:14: - **Scalability**: Distribute read load across multiple replica databases
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:15: - **Performance**: Reduce primary database load by offloading read queries
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:16: - **High Availability**: Continue serving reads even if primary is under maintenance
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:17: - **Cloud-Native**: Leverage managed database replicas (AWS Aurora, Google Cloud SQL, AlloyDB, etc.)

r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:98: Sticky-After-Write
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:99: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:100: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:101: By default, routing ensures **read-your-writes consistency**. After a write operation,
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:102: all subsequent reads use the primary database until the transaction is committed:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:103: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:104: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:105: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:106:     async with session_maker() as session:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:107:         repo = UserRepository(session=session)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:108: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:109:         # Read routes to replica
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:110:         users = await repo.get_many()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:111: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:112:         # Write routes to primary
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:113:         new_user = await repo.add(User(name="Alice"))
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:114: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:115:         # Read now routes to primary (sticky-after-write)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:116:         user = await repo.get(new_user.id)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:117: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:118:         # Commit resets stickiness
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:119:         await session.commit()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:120: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:121:         # Read can use replica again
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:122:         users = await repo.get_many()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:123: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:124: To disable sticky-after-write:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:125: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:126: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:127: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:128:     config = RoutingConfig(
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:129:         primary_connection_string="postgresql+asyncpg://...",
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:130:         read_replicas=["..."],
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:131:         sticky_after_write=False,  # Reads may not see recent writes
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:132:     )
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:133: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:134: Routing Rules
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:135: -------------
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:136: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:137: The routing layer follows these rules:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:138: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:139: 1. **INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE** → Primary
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:140: 2. **SELECT with FOR UPDATE** → Primary
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:141: 3. **SELECT after write** (if sticky-after-write enabled) → Primary
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:142: 4. **SELECT (no writes)** → Replica (round-robin/random)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:143: 5. **After commit** → Reset stickiness, replicas available again
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:144: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:145: FOR UPDATE Detection
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:146: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:147: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:148: Queries with ``FOR UPDATE`` are automatically routed to the primary:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:149: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:150: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:151: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:152:     from sqlalchemy import select
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:153: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:154:     async with session_maker() as session:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:155:         # Routes to primary (FOR UPDATE detected)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:156:         stmt = select(User).where(User.id == user_id).with_for_update()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:157:         result = await session.execute(stmt)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:158:         user = result.scalar_one()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:159: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:160: Advanced Routing with Bind Groups
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:161: ---------------------------------
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:162: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:163: While the primary/read-replica pattern is common, you might need more complex routing scenarios, such as:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:164: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:165: - Dedicated analytics database
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:166: - Region-specific replicas
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:167: - Separate reporting databases
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:168: - Multiple primary databases (sharding)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:169: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:170: You can achieve this by defining **Bind Groups** in your configuration.
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:171: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:172: Configuration
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:173: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:174: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:175: Use the ``engines`` dictionary to define named groups of engines:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:176: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:177: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:178: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:179:     from advanced_alchemy.config import SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:180:     from advanced_alchemy.config.routing import RoutingConfig
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:181: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:182:     config = SQLAlchemyAsyncConfig(
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:183:         routing_config=RoutingConfig(
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:184:             # Define multiple engine groups
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:185:             engines={
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:186:                 "default": ["postgresql+asyncpg://primary:5432/db"],
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:187:                 "read": ["postgresql+asyncpg://replica1:5432/db"],
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:188:                 "analytics": ["postgresql+asyncpg://analytics:5432/db"],
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:189:                 "reporting": [
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:190:                     "postgresql+asyncpg://report-1:5432/db",
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:191:                     "postgresql+asyncpg://report-2:5432/db",
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:192:                 ],
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:193:             },
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:194:             default_group="default",
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:195:             read_group="read",
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:196:         ),
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:197:     )
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:198: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:199: Using Bind Groups
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:200: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:201: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:202: You can route operations to specific groups using context managers or explicit parameters.
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:203: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:204: **Context Manager**
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:205: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:206: Use ``use_bind_group`` to route all operations within a block to a specific group:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:207: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:208: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:209: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:210:     from advanced_alchemy.routing import use_bind_group
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:211: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:212:     async with session_maker() as session:
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:213:         repo = UserRepository(session=session)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:214: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:215:         # Route to analytics database
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:216:         with use_bind_group("analytics"):
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:217:             stats = await repo.count()
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:218: 
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:219:         # Route to reporting group (load balanced if multiple engines)
r2/docs/usage/routing.rst:220:         with use_bind_group("reporting"):

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:151: Repository Integration

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:154: The cache manager integrates with repositories through the ``cache_manager`` parameter:

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:156: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:157:

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:166:         session=session,
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:167:         cache_manager=cache_manager,

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:169:     )

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:173:     users = await repo.get_many()  # Cached with version-based invalidation

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:175: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:176: Bypassing the Cache
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:177: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:178: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:179: You can bypass the cache for specific queries:
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:180: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:181: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:182: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:183:     # Force database fetch, skip cache
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:184:     user = await repo.get(user_id, use_cache=False)

r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:186: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:187: Automatic Cache Invalidation
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:188: ----------------------------
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:189: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:190: When using the config system with ``cache_config``, cache listeners are
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:191: automatically registered (controlled by ``enable_cache_listener=True``, the default).
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:192: Cache entries are automatically invalidated when models are created, updated, or deleted.
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:193: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:194: The invalidation is transaction-aware:
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:195: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:196: - Invalidations are deferred until the transaction commits
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:197: - If the transaction rolls back, invalidations are discarded
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:198: - Entity caches are invalidated by ID
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:199: - List caches use version-based invalidation (bumps a version token)
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:200: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:201: Version-Based List Invalidation
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:202: ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:203: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:204: List queries use version-based invalidation. When any entity of a model type
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:205: is modified, a version token is bumped, which invalidates all list caches
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:206: for that model:
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:207: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:208: .. code-block:: python
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:209: 
r2/docs/usage/caching.rst:210:     # First call caches with version token "abc123"
